children: The Federal Open Market Committee increased its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points on Wednesday, as widely expected, the first rate hike in more than three years.
The adjustment is intended to tamp down demand to rein in inflation, which has exceeded its 2% goal for more than five years. All 12 voting members voted for the rate increase.
The Federal Reserve described the economy as "expanding at a solid pace" with “resilient” domestic spending. Still, uncertainty remained elevated, in part from geopolitical developments.
"Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment is robust," the committee said. "Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little."

title: Federal Reserve hikes rate to 3.75%-4.00%, the first increase in three years
